population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: ever 26.5% − current 18.8% = 7.7% of adults used and are off now. The 10.0 pts of new ever-users since 2028 split into 7.5 on and 2.5 already off. Of the 16.5 pts who had used by 2028, 11.3 are on and 5.2 are off. On: 7.5 + 11.3 = 18.8. Off: 2.5 + 5.2 = 7.7. Within the 2028 cohort: 5.0 of the 9.9 then on stayed on; 4.9 stopped, joining the 6.6 already off for a pool of 11.5; 6.3 of those restarted (55% over two years, consistent with 36–47% within one year); 5.0 + 6.3 = 11.3. Cycled: the 6.6 pts who had cycled by 2028, plus about 2.3 pts of first-time restarts, gives 8.9 of 26.5 ever-users = 34%. That is down from 40% only because the large new-starter cohort dilutes it. Current users are about 50.2M of ~267M adults. Age bands weighted by adult population shares (20/33/24/23%) give 2.0 + 6.6 + 7.4 + 2.8 = 18.8. Income thirds average (25 + 18.5 + 13)/3 = 18.8. Bottom-third use doubled because of three channels: free generic liraglutide at community health centres, cessation and AUD coverage, and gray-market compounded pens. Most bottom-third users take lower-efficacy agents (liraglutide 5–8%, compounded semaglutide of unverified dose). 65+ rose from 8% to 12% (~7.4M) despite the fracture labelling, through Bridge renewal and DEXA-monitored regimens, but stayed below 2026 levels relative to the 50–64 band. Off-drug: ~20.6M adults who used and stopped, plus ~196M who never used. The never-used are increasingly people who opted out, as well as people who could not afford it. Pediatric: ~0.8% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 580k, of whom ≈90k are aged 6–11 since the April 2029 liraglutide label. The oldest adolescent cohorts now have ~7 years of exposure, and no bone-accrual data have been reported.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge renewed (Dec 2029) through 2031. Payment rises from $245 to $275/month to absorb the tariff and shortage repricing; the copay stays $50 and the criteria are unchanged, with a documented DEXA/strength counselling visit for 65+. About 2.3M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 2.3M × $275 × 12 ≈ $7.6B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈15.5% of incretin fills ≈ 7.8M users (7.4M adults 65+ plus ~0.4M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ≈11% ≈ 5.5M users at $275: 5.5M × $275 × 12 ≈ $18.2B/yr combined federal and state. The Indiana and Arkansas adherence waivers are unchanged. The new HRSA Community Incretin Access Program is a grant programme, not insurance. It provides free generic liraglutide through FQHCs and free semaglutide for smoking cessation and AUD through state quitlines and SUD clinics, for ≈3.0M users: 2.0M liraglutide × $85 federal contract × 12 = $2.0B, plus 1.0M semaglutide × $199 × 12 = $2.4B, ≈ $4.4B/yr against a $4.5B FY2030 appropriation.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 70+ semaglutide brands at $8–45/month and the first generic tirzepatide filings. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China sell generic semaglutide. Generic oral semaglutide is available in ~175 countries. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~50.1M users: commercial 35.5% (17.8M), Medicare 15.5% (7.8M), Medicaid 11% (5.5M), HRSA free provision 6% (3.0M), cash/direct 14% (7.0M), gray (compounded, imported or research-peptide) 18% (9.0M) = 100%. Price shock: Novo's 2029 fill-finish recall and the Section 232 tariff final rule pushed TrumpRx/direct cash prices from $245–350 to $349 (semaglutide) and $449 (tirzepatide), and oral starting doses from $149 to $199. Wegovy list is still $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499, still allocated with no cash-portal price. Who pays has not changed structurally. Commercial users nonetheless rose from 11.8M to 17.8M because existing law pulled in the new indications. The ACA preventive mandate requires plans to cover FDA-approved cessation drugs, which now includes semaglutide, for two 90-day courses a year. Mental-health parity requires plans that exclude weight drugs to cover semaglutide for AUD on medical-equivalent terms. Prior-auth AUDIT scores have drifted upward, and plans call this 'indication shopping'. Gray prices: US 503A telehealth 'personalised' compounded semaglutide $129–249; Indian mail pens $8–45 plus shipping; 'research-use' retatrutide vials $120–250, with no prescriber.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached market (driver: none). Survodutide received an FDA complete response letter in Jan 2029 over hepatic-signal questions and manufacturing data; it has been resubmitted, with a decision not before 2031. Amycretin (NDA filed Jun 2028) received a CRL in Oct 2029 tied to the same Novo fill-finish facility findings behind the Wegovy recall; resubmission is pending. MariTide (monthly) phase 3 read out and its BLA was filed Jul 2030, so approval is no earlier than mid-2031. Bimagrumab combinations entered phase 3 in 2029 and are not on the market. The new indications come as supplements to existing drugs: semaglutide for smoking cessation (sNDA May 2028, approved Mar 2029) and AUD (sNDA Aug 2029, priority review, approved Jun 2030), and liraglutide for ages 6–11. The under-12 driver is realised through generic-eligible liraglutide, not newer agents. The incretin market is ≈$135B in 2030: US volume nearly doubled, and the tariff repricing offset ex-US generic erosion.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates are higher among gray-market users who escalate without titration guidance.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established. Persistence after discontinuation remains disputed. MDL 3094 (E.D. Pa.) passed ~42,000 filed and tolled claims by mid-2030, driven by the doubled user base and claimant advertising aimed at compounded-product users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus already labelled. First bellwether verdict Mar 2030. Manufacturers book litigation reserves. FDA declines to add persistent gastroparesis to labels, citing insufficient evidence.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; rising in absolute numbers with retatrutide and research-peptide use.
Long-term data still show no causal confirmation and a low absolute risk. About 6,000 claims were folded into the MDL anyway, so litigation is moving ahead of the science.

Population problem in 65+, about 1.5× sarcopenia criteria after more than 2 years. Most visible in low-efficacy, unmonitored, low-protein users. Monitored affluent users largely offset it with training.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label update (2028) stands. Bridge renewal keeps the counselling-visit requirement. The HRSA programme has no body-composition requirement.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended in 65+ and postmenopausal women. The Senate HELP report (2029) faulted Novo's disclosure. FDA pediatric bone-accrual studies are ongoing, and the 6–11 liraglutide label requires one.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings-section mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. FTC warning letters (2030) to telehealth brands making 'calm/focus' claims; FDA says off-label wellness promotion by non-manufacturers falls outside its labelling authority.

food_and_beverage.state: With nearly one adult in five on the drug, volume losses in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks are about double the 2026–28 rate. Majors cut US volume guidance and accelerate sales of indulgent brands. Protein, fibre and bone-health formats keep growing. Discount grocers report a split basket: more protein in affluent zip codes and less in subsidy-heavy ones.

alcohol.state: The AUD approval and parity coverage reach heavy drinkers, the category's profit core. US spirits volumes fall again and beer contracts. Premium 'one good drink' formats and non-alcoholic lines grow. Tobacco and vape makers report cessation-driven declines, which state excise forecasts now model.

restaurants.state: Fine dining and protein-forward fast casual are adapted and steady. Value-volume chains and buffets in mid-income suburbs close underperforming units. Alcohol attach rates fall across the sector.

apparel.state: Size runs keep widening as bodies move both ways. 'Athletic-cut' tailoring for lean, muscled affluent clients is the growth segment. Plus-size retailers shrink further as bottom-third uptake rises.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios expand into second-tier metros. A gym-floor gray market in research-peptide retatrutide draws FDA letters. Low-cost gyms gain members from subsidy users.

insurance.state: The structure is unchanged, but pharmacy trend runs at ~+14% because the cessation mandate and AUD parity force coverage that weight-loss exclusions had blocked. Employer weight-management coverage drifts from 58% to 57%. Adherence gating spreads to cessation and AUD benefits.

pharma.state: Lilly is the volume and margin leader. Novo is recovering from the recall, the amycretin CRL and HELP findings. Both book MDL reserves in the low billions, and tariff repricing lifted US net prices. The generic liraglutide makers that won the HRSA contracts are the surprise winners.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The question is no longer whether someone is on the drug but what they are on and who pays. A lean, muscled, DEXA-tracked body reads as retatrutide plus a coach: top-third money. A thinner body without much muscle reads as kiosk-weigh-in Medicaid, free liraglutide or a compounded pen. A heavier body reads as uninsured, off on purpose, or between 90-day quit courses.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness and muscle are class uniforms. In Charlotte's banking and fintech workforce, men aged 30–49 wear 'the Charlotte build': retatrutide on allocation through concierge practices, a strength coach and quarterly DEXA. Recruiters admit they notice it. Use in the bottom third doubled, mostly on lower-efficacy or unverified product, so the gap is now less about being on or off and more about the quality of the result.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are smaller across many households. Children on liraglutide at the family table have made 'kid portions' a family-doctor topic. Weddings serve two menus. Bars and tasting rooms sell experiences more than volume.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles state the molecule as well as on or off. 'Reta' signals money, and 'clinic pen' is a mild put-down. Mismatched appetites in mixed couples remain openly discussed.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of every kind is treated as a clinical variable. Since the AUD and cessation approvals, a craving left untreated is read as a choice, and in some workplaces as a liability.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Reduced-pleasure reports hold at ~10–15% of long-term users, dose-dependent. Interim retatrutide anhedonia-scale data are ambiguous. At least a dozen telehealth brands now sell low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo subscriptions ($199–279/month) to people without obesity, explicitly for 'quiet', 'focus' and 'freedom from craving'. An estimated 1.5–2M adults use them, counted inside the cash and gray shares.
interior_life.framing: Sold as a feature. Wellness brands advertise 'the off switch for noise'. Clinicians still say 'dose-dependent reward modulation'. Users who dislike the effect call it 'the grey' and lower their dose. Regulators treat it as advertising, not pharmacology.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers have moved from rewarding observable correlates to subsidising 'focus' subscriptions as a perk in finance, call centres and logistics. Trucking fleets still rely on tirzepatide for DOT apnea clearance. Sales and creative staff still go off-dose before pitches. Unions in three national contracts won language barring employers from viewing PBM adherence data.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Writing off-dose' has become a credited aesthetic: a touring circuit, small-label albums and comedy specials billed as unmedicated. Leisure keeps shifting toward intense, short experiences such as sauna, cold plunge and single tastings. Sports betting operators report softer handle in high-uptake states and say so on earnings calls.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists routinely ask about dose. Couples on 'focus' subscriptions report fewer fights and less wanting, and describe both as true. Dose holidays around anniversaries are a commonplace joke.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Visible on price, tariffs, free provision and torts. Talk-radio hosts on both sides call the HRSA programme 'pacification pills', but no turnout or mood effect is measured. Candidates are asked whether they are 'on'.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on indications (cessation, AUD, ages 6–11) and still defensive on safety: CRLs for survodutide and amycretin, Novo facility enforcement, HELP findings. Gray-market enforcement is selective and largely symbolic once shortage-exception compounding ended. The FTC, not the FDA, polices 'calm/focus' marketing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy: the HRSA Community Incretin Access Program was funded through a bipartisan appropriations rider (Jul 2029, $4.5B for FY2030) and provides free generic liraglutide at FQHCs and free semaglutide through quitlines and SUD clinics. It is discretionary and must be renewed annually. There is no mandate to take the drug. The Medicare Bridge was renewed at $275/$50, and the ACA cessation mandate and parity law now apply to semaglutide.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged: ≥80% PDC and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses. Three more states have applied. HRSA programme sites require only refill pickup, not weigh-ins. That creates a two-tier conditioning system, which waiver plaintiffs cite.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea screening still makes tirzepatide a de facto requirement for some drivers. The Army keeps its contested recruit policy. The VA adopted semaglutide for AUD under the 2029 VA/DoD guideline.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 tariff final rule (Jan 2029) and Novo's US plant failure repriced the branded supply. India's mail-order exports to the US are a standing item in trade talks. Indian API also feeds US 503A compounders, so tariff policy and gray-market supply are tied together.

open_tensions: Free provision, the cessation mandate and AUD parity doubled use among lower-income Americans, mostly on lower-efficacy or unverified product with no body-composition monitoring, while the affluent pay for retatrutide plus a coach. The state is subsidising exactly the regimen the bone and muscle labels warn about.
The gray market is now 18% of users and is fed by the same Indian API the tariff was meant to price out. Enforcement against it would collide with a subsidy programme whose purpose is access.

Reward blunting is sold as a feature, subsidised as an employee perk and approved as a treatment for alcohol and nicotine, but has still not been measured as a harm. The first validated anhedonia data from retatrutide postmarketing studies are due in 2031.
Mass-tort claims are moving ahead of causal evidence on pancreatitis and persistent gastroparesis. Settlement pressure may reshape labels and prices before the science settles.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 a month, is supply-allocated, has no TrumpRx cash price, and carries its bone and body-composition monitoring section.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Free Pills for the Poor, Retatrutide for the Rich: One in Five Americans Is On It, and You Can Tell Who Paid
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 nearly one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, about fifty million people, close to twice the number two years ago. This happened while the price went up. In January 2029 an FDA warning letter shut lines at Novo Nordisk's North Carolina fill-finish plant, semaglutide went onto the shortage list, and the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff took effect in the same month. The cash portal raised semaglutide to $349 a month, tirzepatide to $449 and the starter pill to $199. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, and retatrutide is still $1,499 and rationed.

Three channels carried people past the price. The first was existing law. Semaglutide's smoking-cessation approval in 2029 brought it under the ACA's preventive mandate, and its alcohol-use-disorder approval in June 2030 brought it under mental-health parity. Plans that had refused to pay for weight loss now pay for quitting and for drinking less, two ninety-day courses at a time. Benefits managers watch AUDIT scores creep upward and call it indication shopping.

The second was the state. A bipartisan appropriations rider funded a $4.5 billion federal programme that hands out generic liraglutide free at community health centres and free semaglutide through quitlines and addiction clinics, about three million people in all. Liraglutide is older, daily and weaker, but it is generic and now labelled for children from six. About ninety thousand children under twelve are on a drug, and no one has bone data for them.

The third was the gray market. The shortage briefly made compounding legal again. When it ended, the telehealth pharmacies kept shipping 'personalised doses', gyms began selling vials of retatrutide labelled for research, and Indian pens kept arriving by mail. About nine million Americans use product no American regulator has inspected. The FDA sends letters. Poison-centre calls have doubled.

The result is a country where nearly everyone can get some version of the drug, but the versions differ. In Charlotte's banks, men in their thirties and forties have the same build: retatrutide through a concierge practice, a strength coach, a DEXA scan every quarter. Recruiters notice it, and so does everyone else. Bottom-third use has doubled to thirteen percent, mostly on liraglutide, rationed courses or a compounded pen, and often without muscle monitoring. Thin no longer marks the line between classes. The finish does: muscle, bone and a measured dose. In Gary, Indiana, the Medicaid weigh-in kiosk still decides who keeps coverage. The free clinic down the street asks for nothing but a refill pickup, and the waiver plaintiffs have noticed.

The quieting effect that people named the Ozempic personality in 2026 has become a product. A dozen wellness brands sell low-dose pill subscriptions for 'quiet' and 'freedom from craving' to people who were never heavy, and some employers now pay for them as a perk. The FTC has sent warning letters. Surveys still find that one long-term user in eight feels less pleasure. Musicians bill their tours as off-dose. Sports-betting companies blame softer betting volume on their customers' medication.

The lawsuits arrived with the volume. More than forty thousand gastroparesis and pancreatitis claims sit in a federal courtroom in Philadelphia. A jury found for the first bellwether plaintiff in March. The pancreatitis science still says 'suspected', and the claims keep coming anyway. Spirits makers cut guidance again. Snack makers sell indulgent brands. Both drugmakers report record US revenue. From a distance the country looks calmer and leaner, and it drinks less. Up close, you can tell from someone's body who paid for their drug.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tasha Greer weighs herself on the bathroom scale at 5:40, though nothing rides on that one anymore. She missed two kiosk weigh-ins last winter while working doubles, and Indiana locked her out of Medicaid coverage until March. Her pen comes from a telehealth pharmacy in Florida: $179, a vial, a box of syringes and a dosing card she keeps on the fridge next to Jaylen's spelling list.

Jaylen is nine. His liraglutide is free from the health centre on Broadway, and they never ask him to step on anything. She does his shot at the counter while he eats half a waffle. He says it pinches. She says everything pinches.

By eight she's in Crown Point at Mr. Albrecht's, a retired bank man with a stoop that his coach says is improving. His retatrutide comes in a cooler bag from a concierge doctor. She lays out his protein shake, his calcium and his DEXA printout for Thursday, and helps him through twelve slow squats holding the kitchen counter. He tells her she looks good, lighter. She says thank you and doesn't say what she pays.

At lunch her sister texts a link from a law firm, Stomach problems after Ozempic? Tasha's stomach is fine. She deletes it.

After pickup, Jaylen wants McDonald's and finishes four nuggets before he stops, folds the box and says he's done. She eats his fries without wanting them, out of habit.

At nine she sets the pen supplies out for Sunday and checks the date on the dosing card. She writes 'March' on the calendar in red, then 'kiosk' under it, twice.
